full_judgment:
4. Defendant Nos. 1-5 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable. Momtaz Miah, predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs, sold (12+15)=27 decimals land, i.e. the suit land to Moniruddin, predecessor-in-interest of the defendants for rupees 807.00 and for rupees 1000 respectively by two registered kabalas dated the 11th day of February, 1966 and Moniruddin agreed to reconvey the said respective quantum of lands if Momtaz Miah could repay the money by Magh 1373 B.S. and by Magh 1377 B.S. and accordingly, he executed and registered two agreements in that respect. It was also agreed that if the vendor-Momtaz Miah failed to return the kabala money within the prescribed period, the respective transaction became out and out sale after the stipulated period. As Momtaz Miah and his people threatened to dispossess Moniruddin from the suit land, he (Moniruddin) filed Title Suit No. 90 of 1979 in the Court of Munsif, Third Court, for permanent injunction which was decreed on contest on 31.08.1995. Against the Judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No.90 of 1979, Momtaz Miah filed Title Appeal No. 187 of 1985 before the District Judge, Noakhali which was dismissed on contest on 7th October, 1985. Tenure of reconveyance expired long before the promulgation of the Presidential Orders were not applicable in the present case. The defendants as the heirs of Moniruddin have been possessing the suit land by exercising their absolute right and title therein. The plaintiffs were not entitled to get redemption of the suit land as it was not a mortgage and that it was not redeemed in time as per the agreement in time as such, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 6. The trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 27.09.2005 dismissed the suit on the finding, inter alia, that the transactions became past and closed long before the insertion of section 95A in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act, 1950) and as such, the said section had no manner of application; the plaintiffs failed to prove that their predecessor-in-interest paid back the kabala money and got back possession of the suit land that subsequently, they were dispossessed by the defendants; since the plaintiffs claimed that in payment of the kabala money by their predecessor-in-interest, he got back possession of the suit land, but subsequently, Moniruddin did not execute and register the deed of reconveyance, the suit for redemption was not maintainable and the plaintiffs ought to have filed the suit for specific performance of contact. 

 "the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division committed an error of law in not considering that Safkabalas and agreements to reconvey dated 11.02.1966 and tenure of agreement relating to Safkabala No. 1246 was 4 years and tenure of another agreement relating to Safkabala No. 1247 was 5 years and the tenure of the agreement expired on 11.02.1970 and 11.02.1971 respectively long before President's Order No. 88 of 1972 inserting Section 95A to the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was inserted which was made on 03.08.1972 and as such transactions relating to the suit land was past and closed at the time of making of P.O. 88 of 1972 and as such it did not hit the transaction relating to the suit land in view of the law laid down in the cases reported in 1 BLC(AD) 164, 32 DLR (AD) 233, 1 DCC(AD) 60, 33 DLR(AD) 233 and 2008 (XVI) BLT (AD) 357 and therefore the Judgment and Order passed by the High Court Division are not sustainable in law" and "Regard being had to the fact that in order to attract Section 58(e) (sic, it would be 58(c)) of Transfer of Property Act to a transaction the condition is to be embodied in the sale deed but in the present case no such condition of redemption was contained in the sale deed as such the present transaction is an out and out sale and it cannot be treated as mortgage and the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division committed an error of law in discharging the Rule without considering this aspect of the case and therefore, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division are not sustainable in law." 

 8. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, learned Counsel for the appellants, in fact, has made his submissions elaborating the grounds on which leave was granted. Therefore, we need not restate his submissions as that would be absolutely nothing but repetition.
